author: EmuCore - Hub
title: The PlayStation 2: All About Emotion
summary: VideoGameDocs traces the PlayStation 2's launch, architecture and software ecosystem in a feature-length retrospective that gives emulation choices historical context.

blocks.text: This documentary takes a broad route through the PS2's arrival after the first PlayStation, the commercial expectations around its launch and the hardware decisions behind its library. It is a useful companion to narrower technical videos because it places the Emotion Engine and Graphics Synthesizer beside the system's disc format, backward compatibility and developer ecosystem. These choices shaped what games were built and why their assumptions still matter to preservation.

A retrospective necessarily compresses a long generation into a single narrative. Dates and sales totals should be checked against contemporary Sony records when precise chronology matters, and an example game should not stand in for the entire library. View it for the relationships between hardware, software and adoption, then follow the original documents for exact regional launches or specifications. Its strongest contribution to an emulation catalog is explaining why faithful PS2 behavior includes more than faster rendering.
